subject: Clarify: customer asks for regional lock + no-fallback + specific model variant
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sophie Reinhart <sophie@atlashealth.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Customer ask: region lock + no-fallback + variant binding (Atlas Health)

Sophie (and Atlas team),

Thanks for the detailed deck — quick summary for the internal folks below. Atlas Health is asking for three hard constraints for their pilot:

1) EU-only serving (data must remain in eu-west1 region).
2) No automatic fallback chaining — if the pinned model variant isn't available we must return an error rather than route to a lower-cost/compat model.
3) Force use of a specific quantized variant for predictability (they mentioned “redwood/galen-8q” as the required variant).

Attached: atlas_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet of asks), sso_policy.pdf (their SSO/SCIM requirements).

Internal: Laura/Karthik/Monica/Marissa — can you confirm the following by EOD?
- Product: is a hard model+region bind supported today (console + API flag) and what are the UX/rollout implications?
- Ops: if we must enforce NO-FALLBACK, what are the availability implications and what needs to change in routing? Estimate infra lead time and any pricing delta.
- Security/Legal: what additional controls or paperwork (DPA, SOC evidence, KMS) do we require before we sign on for a no-fallback contract?

Sophie — if you can confirm that the variant is non-negotiable and whether a dedicated Dedicated pool or Private deployment is acceptable, that will help us give a concrete plan.

Thanks,
Alex
Product Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments: atlas_requirements.xlsx (xlsx), sso_policy.pdf (pdf)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Sophie Reinhart <sophie@atlashealth.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Customer ask: region lock + no-fallback + variant binding (Atlas Health)

Thanks Alex — looping Product here.

On the surface: we can gate by region and expose a model_pin flag today, but there are two important product trade-offs to call out:

- UX: our current pinned-model behavior allows an "on-fallback" policy (fallback -> compatible variant) or a hard error. We can flip to hard error but it is a change to default routing behavior and will require a config surface on the route (we already have a feature flag in staging).
- Capacity & availability: if we pin to a single variant in a single region, customer-facing latency SLOs will be vulnerable to transient infra issues. If Atlas cannot tolerate fallback we should strongly recommend a Dedicated pool (reserved capacity) or Private deployment.

Questions for Atlas (Sophie):
1) Is the requirement that requests must fail immediately when the pinned variant is not available, or is a queue/retry acceptable for short windows?
2) Do you require persistent session affinity to that variant?

Action: I'll draft config changes and a proposed rollout (canary in one EU hostzone). Need Ops/Infra ETA for Dedicated pooling.

- Laura
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 13:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Customer ask: region lock + no-fallback + variant binding (Atlas Health)

Short answer: region lock OK, no-fallback raises compliance + contractual considerations.

Details:
- Data residency: serving in eu-west1 is fine, but we need Atlas to sign the DPA amendment explicitly stating EU residency and log retention limits.
- KMS/HSM: if they insist on a specific variant because of deterministic outputs tied to regulatory processing, we should require a KMS-backed key for any customer-side encryption and ensure audit logging is enabled.
- No-fallback risk: operationally, no-fallback increases the chance of service disruption for their end-users. From a security and compliance perspective, we must build an incident response runbook that includes how we escalate availability incidents and share post-incident forensics.

Requests from Security:
1) Atlas to provide SOC2 or equivalent auditor contact; if not available, a Scoped Security Assessment will be required prior to go-live.
2) Legal to review the amendment language that codifies NO-FALLBACK behavior and liability.
3) Ops to confirm whether we can provide immutable audit logs for the pinned route (read-only exports to Atlas SIEM).

I'll attach a short checklist separately (sending to Alex and Marissa).

- Monica
Security Lead, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Customer ask: region lock + no-fallback + variant binding (Atlas Health)

Thanks everyone — operational summary and proposed next steps.

Summary of constraints received: EU-only, force model redwood/galen-8q, no-fallback -> fail-fast.

Implications / ETA:
- Infrastructure: we can provision a dedicated pool in eu-west1 and hard-pin routing to a single variant. Reserving GPUs and capacity for an enterprise customer will take ~3 business days (we need a signed commitment and capacity window).
- Availability: with a dedicated pool we can meet Atlas's availability SLA for the window, but no-fallback still exposes them to single-variant failures; we recommend a 72-hour canary with SLO monitoring before expanding traffic.
- Pricing: committing dedicated pool + hard-fail semantics will require a pricing amendment (est. +27% uplift in monthly unit price). Legal/Finance needs to sign the amendment.
- Playbook: Ops will produce a canary runbook and incident escalation matrix. I created a working folder (link above) with a draft runbook and will add the runbook PDF post-review.

Action items (owners):
- Marissa (Legal): draft DPA amendment + no-fallback liability clause (ETA 48 hours).
- Monica (Security): confirm SOC2 evidence or scoped assessment requirement (ETA 24 hours).
- Laura (Product): finalize config change and create staging flag; confirm canary metrics (ETA 48 hours).
- Alex (Solutions): get Atlas confirmation on variant non-negotiable and sign-off on dedicated pool (ETA: Sophie to confirm by EOD tomorrow).
- Karthik (Ops): block capacity and prepare canary runbook once legal gives go-ahead.

Sophie — please confirm whether Atlas prefers Dedicated or a Private deployment for the pilot; if Dedicated, we need a written commitment to proceed with provisioning.

I'll follow up with a short Ops playbook and a DocuSign amendment template once Legal posts the draft.

- Karthik
Head of Dedicated Operations, Redwood Inference
